Uninstall programs and Store apps you pick
Desktop programs run their own uninstallers, one at a time; Store apps are removed for this Windows account. Both are permanent, and a second list then offers what they left behind.
Leftovers of uninstalled programs

What uninstalled programs left where nothing installed, registered or running still uses it. Needs administrator permission. Folders and shortcuts go to the Recycle Bin; everything else is backed up first.
Windows updates
Windows updates you pick
Security, quality and Defender updates and the malicious software removal tool, as Windows Update lists them for this PC. Windows Update fetches each one; windowsweep never restarts your PC.
drivers
Driver updates and old driver packages

Driver updates from Windows Update, and old packages left in the driver store. The newest two of each driver always stay, so Device Manager’s Roll Back keeps working. BIOS and firmware updates are never offered, and your PC maker’s own driver tool is named, never run.
app updates
App updates you pick
winget fetches each update from its publisher, one at a time. An app that is running is skipped, and an installer that changes the whole PC may show its own Windows permission prompt.
